headlines.text: That Saturday in 2019, the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as Chris Jericho vs. Cody went to war, appearing on Full Gear, rated 8.20 ? one of the better matches of the year. For Cody, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. A defining moment in AEW's early history ? Cody's best friend MJF threw in the towel to end the match, then kicked Cody in the groin as a full-on heel turn, a moment that got over huge with the live crowd chanting in disbelief.
2022 brought us this moment: The Gunn Club left that name behind for good, stepping out as The Gunns after 11 matches under the old identity, on Dynamite.

Rewind to 2024, when Castagnoli, PAC & Yuta vs. Briscoe, Ishii & O'Reilly clashed for the AEW World Trios Titles, appearing on Collision, rated 6.87. It was the first title opportunity of Briscoe, Ishii & O'Reilly's career. Championship gold always raises the stakes.

secondaries.text: It was 2019 when Jon Moxley vs. Kenny Omega fought it out in a Lights Out match, in the night's main event on Full Gear, rated 8.96 ? a genuine showstealer in a hard-fought men's division clash ? part of a stacked Full Gear '19 card, rated 8.06 overall. An unsanctioned, nearly 40-minute war of pure violence ? barbed wire bats, broken glass, and mousetraps all came into play before Moxley finally put Omega away, in a match still remembered as one of the most brutal in AEW's history.
Flash back to 2019, when Proud-N-Powerful stepped through the curtain for the first time as a team, appearing on Full Gear, rated 7.45 ? a match that delivered.

Looking back to 2022, when Bryan Danielson vs. Sammy Guevara settled things in a 2 out of 3 Falls match, serving as the night's main event on Dynamite, rated 7.83 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle in a hard-fought men's division clash.
